findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition overrides the first, breaking existing callers
findings.body: `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined at line 149. Ruby has no overloading, so the second silently replaces the first. Any existing caller using the 4-positional-arg form (`downsize(from, to, 100, 100, opts)`) now passes `max_height` as the `opts` argument. `optimize` then reads `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer, which is a bug, and the dimensions are wrong. The first definition is dead code. Keep one signature and update callers.

findings.title: Downsizing loop can run needlessly and uses the wrong extension/animation handling
findings.body: The loop runs ImageMagick on `tempfile.path` in place, up to 5 times. When `convert` fails, `downsize` returns false and the file is unchanged, but the loop keeps retrying five times, each time spawning a process. The result is never checked. If the image is still too large afterwards, it proceeds to `Upload.create_for`, which presumably rejects it, but only after wasted work. Also, `tempfile.size` may be cached or stale after an external process rewrites the file, because it is a Ruby File/Tempfile object. `File.size(tempfile.path)` would be safer. The animated-GIF path (gifsicle) is chosen by the `.GIF` extension of the temp path. Rails tempfile names often lack the original extension, so animation handling will not trigger as intended. Stop the loop when the downsize returns false.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings and the 413 message is inaccurate
findings.body: The client-side limit was changed from `max_<type>_size_kb` to a hardcoded 10MB. This applies to attachments as well as images, so the `max_attachment_size_kb` setting is no longer enforced on the client. Attachments over the configured limit but under 10MB now pass the client check. Nothing in this diff shows the server enforcing it. The same hardcoding appears in the 413 handler (line 246). The error message reports a limit that may differ from the actual server limit. The magic number is duplicated in the JS and in the controller (`10.megabytes`).

findings.title: API download limit hardcoded and `tempfile` nil not handled
findings.body: The URL download limit was changed from the site setting to a fixed 10MB, so admins' configured limits are no longer honoured for API URL uploads. If the download fails, `tempfile` is nil because of `rescue nil`. The new guard handles nil, but `tempfile.size` on line 72 will still raise NoMethodError. This pre-existing problem is now more visible, since the new block is guarded for nil while the next line is not.

findings.title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior
findings.body: The new automatic downsizing path, the refactored `optimize`/`downsize` signature, and the removed `dimensions` helper have no accompanying tests. This is a behavioral change in upload handling that touches shell-invoked image processing.
